The goal of this 24 week double-blinded, randomized, parallel controlled clinical trial is to learn how semaglutide affects body composition in adults with type 1 diabetes and overweight/obesity.

record.brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if supervised exercise training combined with a daily protein supplement can reduce the loss of muscle mass and muscle strength in adults with type 2 diabetes who have recently started treatment with semaglutide or tirzepatide. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the exercise and protein program reduce the loss of thigh muscle volume over 24 weeks?
* Does the program improve muscle strength, physical fitness, insulin sensitivity and liver lipids?

Researchers will compare participants who take part in the exercise and protein program to participants who receive usual care only, to see if the program helps to preserve skeletal muscle during treatment-related weight loss.

All participants will:

* Continue their semaglutide or tirzepatide treatment as prescribed by their own doctor
* Receive one lifestyle counselling session on nutrition and physical activity at the start of the study
* Attend two study visits, at the start and after 24 weeks, each lasting two days, including MRI scans, body composition measurement, blood tests, an insulin sensitivity test (clamp), small muscle and fat tissue samples, and tests of muscle strength and fitness
* Collect their urine over 24 hours before each study visit
* Keep a food diary and complete questionnaires at the start and after 6, 12, 18 and 24 weeks

Participants in the exercise and protein group will also:

* Take part in supervised exercise training (strength and interval training) three times per week for 24 weeks
* Drink a protein shake (whey protein) every day

record.brief_summary: This clinical study investigates how blocking the hunger-related ghrelin receptor affects appetite and metabolism in individuals with obesity who are treated with semaglutide (a GLP-1 receptor agonist). LEAP2, a naturally occurring hormone that inhibits the ghrelin receptor, is used as the investigational compound. The objective of the study is to clarify how the ghrelin system functions when appetite is suppressed by semaglutide treatment. Participants will receive either LEAP2 or placebo during two experimental visits in a randomized, double-blind, crossover design. The investigators will assess food intake, appetite sensations, glucose metabolism, and hormonal responses. By examining the interaction between semaglutide and ghrelin signaling, the study aims to improve understanding of how multiple appetite-regulating systems interact and whether additional hunger signals remain active during GLP-1 treatment. The findings may inform the development of future treatments for individuals with obesity.

record.brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to assess the effect and effectiveness of Relacorilant on improving the glucose levels in the blood, thus potentially improving glucose control in patients with hard to control diabetes.

This study involves the use of an investigational drug called Relacorilant. "Investigational" means that the drug has not yet been approved by the U.S. Food \& Drug Administration (FDA) for treating "mild hypercortisolism" in patients with diabetes. Cortisol is a "stress hormone". The excess production of cortisol can rise blood sugar (glucose) levels and worsen diabetes. Those disturbances might be corrected by the study medication Relacorilant to improve the state of your diabetes.

What effect does Semaglutide have on body composition in adults with type 1 diabetes and overweight/obesity compared to a placebo?

* Be randomly assigned to receive semaglutide or a placebo.
* Self-administer the treatment drug once per week for 24 weeks.
* Complete a series of tests, measurements and questionnaires throughout the study duration.
* Attend a remote follow-up visit 4 weeks after the treatment is complete.

record.brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if supervised exercise training combined with a daily protein supplement can reduce the loss of muscle mass and muscle strength in adults with type 2 diabetes who have recently started treatment with semaglutide or tirzepatide. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does the exercise and protein program reduce the loss of thigh muscle volume over 24 weeks?
* Does the program improve muscle strength, physical fitness, insulin sensitivity and liver lipids?

Researchers will compare participants who take part in the exercise and protein program to participants who receive usual care only, to see if the program helps to preserve skeletal muscle during treatment-related weight loss.

All participants will:

* Continue their semaglutide or tirzepatide treatment as prescribed by their own doctor
* Receive one lifestyle counselling session on nutrition and physical activity at the start of the study
* Attend two study visits, at the start and after 24 weeks, each lasting two days, including MRI scans, body composition measurement, blood tests, an insulin sensitivity test (clamp), small muscle and fat tissue samples, and tests of muscle strength and fitness
* Collect their urine over 24 hours before each study visit
* Keep a food diary and complete questionnaires at the start and after 6, 12, 18 and 24 weeks

Participants in the exercise and protein group will also:

* Take part in supervised exercise training (strength and interval training) three times per week for 24 weeks
* Drink a protein shake (whey protein) every day

record.brief_summary:
This study will assess whether women with obesity and early estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer can complete 26 weeks of semaglutide treatment while continuing their prescribed hormone therapy for breast cancer. The researchers expect that semaglutide can be given alongside hormone therapy with good treatment adherence. The study will also examine side effects, weight changes, body composition, metabolic health and quality of life.

Thirty-two women will be randomly assigned to start semaglutide immediately or after a 26-week waiting period. Both groups will continue usual breast cancer care and receive written advice about diet and physical activity. Semaglutide will be self-injected under the skin once a week for 26 weeks, with the dose increased gradually according to tolerability.

Participants will attend visits for weight and body measurements, blood tests, side-effect assessments and questionnaires. Follow-up will continue for 26 weeks after the treatment period. Total follow-up from randomization will be 52 weeks for the immediate-start group and 78 weeks for the delayed-start group. Some participants will also be invited to interviews about their experience of treatment.
record.brief_title: Semaglutide for Weight Management During Hormone Therapy for Early Breast Cancer

eligibility.criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Female diagnosed with estrogen receptor-positive early breast cancer (stage I-III).
2. Currently receiving, or planning to initiate, adjuvant endocrine therapy for early estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, with at least 78 weeks of planned endocrine therapy remaining at randomization.
3. Body mass index of at least 30 kg/m² at screening.
4. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status 0-1.
5. Age 18 years or older.
6. Able to provide oral and written informed consent in Danish.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Ongoing treatment with semaglutide or another GLP-1 receptor agonist, or previous use of any pharmacological weight-reducing agent within the last 6 months.
2. Type 1 or type 2 diabetes mellitus, or HbA1c of at least 48 mmol/mol.
3. Self-reported alcohol intake exceeding 14 units per week, or severe substance abuse.
4. Known pregnancy at screening.
5. Women of childbearing potential who are unable or unwilling to use contraception.
6. Significant somatic disease, defined as any of the following:

   * End-stage renal failure with estimated glomerular filtration rate below 15 mL/min/1.73 m².
   * Alanine or aspartate aminotransferase above twice the upper limit of normal.
   * History of acute or chronic pancreatitis.
   * Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2.
   * New York Heart Association class IV heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, or myocardial infarction within the previous 6 months.
   * Uncontrolled hypertension, defined as systolic blood pressure above 180 mmHg or diastolic blood pressure above 100 mmHg.
7. Currently breastfeeding.
8. Women of childbearing potential who are unable or unwilling to use an effective contraceptive method during semaglutide treatment and for at least 2 months after the last dose.
9. Current participation in another interventional drug trial.
10. Any circumstance that, in the investigator's judgment, would interfere with trial conduct, participant safety or the validity of trial outcomes.
